summary.intent: Improve paging and hint behavior of a search/results CLI (PR #112) so agents can page through all results and understand what the default relevance cut hides, while coordinating several parallel subagents and PRs.
summary.outcome: A subagent clarified that the total T counts rows below the relevance cut and changed the last-page hint to `--min-score 0 for the N rows below the cut`, adding a walk test and updating docs/changeset; checks passed and PR #112 is mergeable with CI restarted and pending. The diff itself was not reviewed.

repo: In the paged output, `showing N of T` counts every match including rows below the relevance cut, so T can exceed the rows reachable with the default cut.
`next: --offset` is only emitted while surviving (above-cut) rows remain, so it never leads to an empty page.
Paging behavior is documented in §47, the architecture doc, and a changeset; all three must be updated when hints change.
Verification suite for changes: `just lint`, `test`, `rg-compare`, `changesets`, `bench`, plus Entire findings check.
workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output without user authority; results should be relayed as the agent's claims, noting the diff was not independently read.
Pushing to a PR restarts CI, so merge readiness should wait for checks to go green again.
A walk test (paging through all pages and comparing to a single large run) is a good way to validate pagination invariants.
